title: What the ZPA Terraform provider sends and loses when writing policy rules
aliases: zpa policy rule update clears fields

prose.text: The ZPA provider builds every rule resource's create and update from Terraform state alone and sends it through SDK helpers that change it further. Ordering of rules is covered in [[zpa.terraform.rule-order]]; deleting objects that rules refer to is covered in [[zpa.terraform.delete-paths]]. This subject is about what a single rule write contains.

v1-update-sends-fresh-request.statement: The v1 forwarding rule update builds its request from Terraform state only and does not read the existing rule to merge: its expander sets a handful of scalar fields and the conditions, and its update calls the SDK without a preceding read. The SDK request type tags `devicePostureFailureNotificationEnabled`, `appServerGroups`, `appConnectorGroups` and `serviceEdgeGroups` without `omitempty`, so they are always serialized, including when the provider left them unset.

import-accepts-types-crud-ignores-them.statement: The access rule importers (v1 and v2) accept the policy types `ACCESS_POLICY` and `GLOBAL_POLICY`, and the timeout rule importers accept `TIMEOUT_POLICY` and `REAUTH_POLICY`. Read always resolves the policy set for `ACCESS_POLICY` or `TIMEOUT_POLICY` and writes `policy_set_id` (the resolved set's ID, except the v1 timeout rule, which writes the policy set ID from the rule it read); in the v1 resources, create, update and delete use a configured `policy_set_id` first, and the v2 resources resolve the fixed type unconditionally. A numeric import ID never consults the types; they matter only for lookup by name.

credential-empty-block-keeps-remote.conditions: Follows from the fallback running before the final ID check and from the read returning the rule's current association; an empty block expands to no credential because the expander sets one only when the id is not empty.

api-put-semantics.title: How the ZPA policy rule PUT treats null, omitted and false fields
api-put-semantics.blocks: saying whether a routine policy rule update clears associations or the credential, or only changes what it names
api-put-semantics.detail: The client sends `null` association lists and `false` flags (or omits a credential field). No captured source states whether the API replaces the whole rule or merges. Test in a scratch tenant: create a rule with server groups and a device-posture flag set, update only its description through the provider, and re-read the rule; repeat with a credential rule, switching credential to pool.

api-idp-operand-shape.title: How the ZPA v2 policy rule response represents IDP and workload tag conditions
api-idp-operand-shape.blocks: saying that refreshed state loses these conditions rather than the response already omitting them
api-idp-operand-shape.detail: The converter drops operands by object type. Create a v2 rule with an IDP condition and a workload tag group condition in a scratch tenant, read it back with the v2 and v1 endpoints, and compare the operand object types.

api-policy-set-types.blocks: saying whether an imported rule is found by the type the provider hardcodes
api-policy-set-types.detail: Fetch the policy set for each of the four type names in a scratch tenant and compare the policy set IDs.
